summary: Sophisticated T1 module — OPEN + NOTIFICATION parsing yields deterministic no-auth proof, expected-AS disclosure, and Router-ID pivot. Never sends UPDATE (correct read-only posture). Biggest gaps: bgp_router_id_pivot should auto-enqueue the new address as a scan target; bgp_no_neighbor_auth doesn't attempt the actual session establishment + prefix injection that would be T2/T3 (which is intentional — destructive). GTSM TTL probe absent. TCP-MD5 detection is a hint (needs raw sockets).

findings.tier_evidence: Reachability confirmation — parseable BGP frame returned.
findings.promotion_notes: Already crosses into T1 by virtue of the OPEN exchange proving unauthenticated peering below. Consumer of known_hosts surface for follow-on scans of Router-ID targets.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap --script bgp-info -p 179 <ip>; then correlate peer AS with whois -h whois.arin.net 'a AS<n>' for ownership.

findings.tier_evidence: Peer replied its own OPEN with no TCP-MD5/TCP-AO/GTSM requirement — deterministic session-setup evidence.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 route injection = actual UPDATE with a benign /32 more-specific into the RIB (measurable via looking-glass, provable). Very destructive on production — must be strictly opt-in --active-bgp-inject with victim address chosen by operator. exabgp harness scripted as tester_next_step is the correct current posture.
findings.tester_next_step: exabgp with 'neighbor <ip> {local-as <expected>; peer-as <peer_asn>; router-id 192.0.2.1; family {inet unicast;} static { route 198.51.100.0/32 next-hop self; }}' — verify at looking-glass; do NOT run without written ROE.

findings.title_pattern: BGP peer discloses expected local AS via NOTIFICATION 'Bad Peer AS'
findings.tier_evidence: Peer's NOTIFICATION data field parsed to extract the configured neighbor AS — deterministic proof of RFC-4271 §6.2 disclosure behaviour.
findings.promotion_notes: Combined with bgp_no_neighbor_auth this IS the T2 primitive — automate a full-OPEN success using the disclosed AS as proof-of-hijack-readiness (session establishes but recce KEEPALIVEs only, no UPDATE). Requires opt-in flag.
findings.tester_next_step: With disclosed AS pair, exabgp neighbor <ip> {peer-as <peer>; local-as <expected>; router-id 192.0.2.1;} — session comes up = full-hijack primitive.

findings.title_pattern: BGP peer identification extracted (AS, version, hold-time, Router-ID, capabilities)
findings.tier_evidence: Parsed OPEN fields — fingerprint disclosure only.
findings.promotion_notes: Consume peer AS into shared known_asns surface for whois attribution and cross-host BGP peering detection.
findings.tester_next_step: whois -h whois.arin.net 'a AS<peer_asn>'; check bgp.tools/<peer_asn> for peering graph.

findings.title_pattern: BGP Router-ID reveals additional host address
findings.tier_evidence: Router-ID IPv4 differs from connected interface — pure discovery.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-enqueue Router-ID as a scan target and mark it as management/loopback — mgmt interfaces almost always accept SSH/HTTPS with weaker ACLs than the data plane.

findings.tier_evidence: Pure informational — capability code + name list.
findings.promotion_notes: No natural promotion path — fingerprint only.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap --script bgp-info -p 179 <ip>; compare cap set against vendor stacks (Cisco IOS-XR advertises Enhanced Route Refresh; FRR advertises LLGR).

findings.tier_evidence: Pure fingerprint — role tag (edge vs PE vs EVPN leaf).
findings.promotion_notes: Consume as role tag in shared os_fingerprints surface; EVPN or L3VPN AFI on a scanned host = data-center fabric leaf, elevates severity of the reachable finding.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap --script bgp-info -p 179 <ip>; if EVPN present, scan for L2/L3 tenant boundary bypass with e.g. VXLAN scanner.

findings.tier_evidence: Pure fingerprint — non-zero restart time hints production vs lab.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap --script bgp-info -p 179 <ip>  # note restart_time; large value = production.

findings.title_pattern: BGP NOTIFICATION reply leaked peer configuration
findings.tier_evidence: NOTIFICATION data field parsed and content extracted — deterministic disclosure.
findings.promotion_notes: Already tightly coupled to bgp_expected_as_disclosed; keep as separate high-signal enum. Consume disclosed values into scan targets.
findings.tester_next_step: Parse leaked value from finding; use in bgp_expected_as_disclosed follow-up.

findings.title_pattern: BGP peer discloses maximum supported version
findings.tier_evidence: Send version=5 OPEN, parse NOTIFICATION 2/1 data field — fingerprint.

findings.title_pattern: BGP peer accepted TCP but did not reply to OPEN (possible TCP-MD5 / ACL requirement)
findings.tier_evidence: Inference from silent drop — recce cannot disambiguate MD5 vs ACL from userspace.
findings.promotion_notes: Requires raw-socket TCP-MD5 probe (RFC 2385 option 19) to confirm — root privilege + raw sockets, non-portable. Alternatively, correlate with a source-address ACL test from a different vantage.
findings.tester_next_step: sudo tcpdump -ni any 'host <ip> and tcp port 179'; retry with 'ip xfrm policy' + TCP-MD5 configured to disambiguate.
